messages.subject: Axivity csv files in G.shell
parts:
Hi Vincent\GGIR users,
First, thanks very much for GGIR!
I would be so grateful if anyone can tell me where I am going wrong trying to read custom csv files into GGIR. Below is an example using the sample axivity .cwa file from UK Biobank website.  The cwa file runs in GGIR no problem, but I can't run the csv I exported in the OMGUI (without resampling, in g)

I am using R version 4.2.1 and GGIR_2.8-2

It seems to work fine for read.myacc.csv(), but this is the error message when I pass to g.part1:

Loading chunk: 1 2Error in which(data[, 1] == 0 & data[, 2] == 0 & data[, 3] == 0) :
  'list' object cannot be coerced to type 'double'
In addition: Warning message:
  In value[[jj]][ri] <- if (is.factor(xij)) as.vector(xij) else xij :
  number of items to replace is not a multiple of replacement length

This is the data format of the csv file, there are no column labels or header
13/07/2013 10:00    -0.03125    -0.125    0.890625

Here is the read.myacc.csv code that works.
read.myacc.csv(rmc.file="accsamp2.csv",
               rmc.nrow=Inf,
               rmc.skip = c(),
               rmc.dec=".",
               rmc.firstrow.acc = 1,
               #rmc.firstrow.header=c(),
               #rmc.header.length = c(),
               rmc.col.acc = c(2:4),
               rmc.col.temp = c(),
               rmc.col.time= 1,
               rmc.unit.acc = "g",
               rmc.unit.temp = "C",
               rmc.unit.time = "POSIX",
               rmc.format.time = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%OS",
               #rmc.bitrate = c(),
               #rmc.dynamic_range = c(),
               #rmc.unsignedbit = TRUE,
               rmc.origin = "1970-01-01",
               rmc.desiredtz = "Europe/London",
               rmc.sf = 100,
               #rmc.headername.sf = c(),
               #rmc.headername.sn = c(),
               #rmc.headername.recordingid = c(),
               #rmc.header.structure = c(),
               rmc.check4timegaps = TRUE,
               #rmc.col.wear = c(),
               #rmc.doresample=FALSE,
               #interpolationType=1,
               PreviousLastValue = c(0, 0, 1),
               PreviousLastTime = NULL,
               epochsize = NULL)    

Here is the output of read.myacc.csv:
  $data
timestamp      accx      accy     accz
1   2013-07-13 10:00:05 -0.031250 -0.109375 0.843750
2   2013-07-13 10:00:05 -0.046875 -0.125000 0.890625
...
$header
[1] "no header"

$PreviousLastValue
[1] -0.031250 -0.125000  0.890625

$PreviousLastTime
[1] "2013-07-13 23:58:33 BST"

Here is the g.part1 code that doesn't work and that gives the error above:


g.part1(datadir <- datadir,
        outputdir = outputdir,
        f0 = 1,
        f1 = 0,
        studyname = "trial",
        #rmc.nrow=Inf,
        #rmc.skip = c(),
        rmc.dec=".",
        rmc.firstrow.acc = 1,
        #rmc.firstrow.header=c(),
        #rmc.header.length = c(),
        rmc.col.acc = c(2:4),
        rmc.col.temp = c(),
        rmc.col.time= 1,
        rmc.unit.acc = "g",
        rmc.unit.temp = "C",
        rmc.unit.time = "POSIX",
        rmc.format.time = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%OS",
        #rmc.bitrate = c(),
        #rmc.dynamic_range = c(),
        #rmc.unsignedbit = TRUE,
        rmc.origin = "1970-01-01",
        rmc.desiredtz = "Europe/London",
        rmc.sf = 100,
        #rmc.headername.sf = c(),
        #rmc.headername.sn = c(),
        #rmc.headername.recordingid = c(),
        #rmc.header.structure = c(),
        #rmc.check4timegaps = TRUE,
        #rmc.col.wear = c(),
        #rmc.doresample=FALSE,
        #interpolationType=1,
        #PreviousLastValue = c(0, 0, 1),
        PreviousLastTime = NULL,
        epochsize = NULL)
)

Any help would be greatly appreciated, 
Thanks,
Cathy

parts:
Hi Cathy,

Why are you trying to process the csv file and not the cwa file?

Please use function GGIR instead of g.part1 as explained in the package vignette. 

"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%OS" is a different time format than what you show in the data.

Best,

Vincent

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: Axivity csv files in G.shell
parts:
Hi Cathy,

You are using rmc.check4timegaps =TRUE in the read.myacc.csv attempt and you do not use it in your GGIR() attempt. Please make sure the arguments are consistent. 

  • Commenting arguments out with # does not reset them to default, they will only be reset to default if you delete the corresponding config.csv file in the output folder, because GGIR falls back on the config.csv file, if present, before falling back to the defaults inside the code.
  • Axivity devices had the problem that they started with a few seconds of zero's in the file. I am not sure, but possibly this can now be handled with rmc.check4timegaps =TRUE.
  • You will need to set rmc.doresample to TRUE because you exported the data without resampling, and GGIR wants a consistent sample rate throughout the recording.

Note that .cwa files are probably more compact to store than the compressed csv files, but I guess either way should be useful for research.

Regarding Jairo's comment - At some point I tried to facilitate Axivity csv format and it may still work, but I later  realised that OMGUI facilitates a lot of sub versions of csv format and it felt tricky to try to auto-detect all those variations. The read.myacc.csv route would seem more practical as you as a user will be in control of how the file is handled.

Best,

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/

On Wednesday, February 15, 2023 at 3:27:13 PM UTC Vincent van Hees wrote:
Hi Cathy,

You are using rmc.check4timegaps =TRUE in the read.myacc.csv attempt and you do not use it in your GGIR() attempt. Please make sure the arguments are consistent. 

  • Commenting arguments out with # does not reset them to default, they will only be reset to default if you delete the corresponding config.csv file in the output folder, because GGIR falls back on the config.csv file, if present, before falling back to the defaults inside the code.
  • Axivity devices had the problem that they started with a few seconds of zero's in the file. I am not sure, but possibly this can now be handled with rmc.check4timegaps =TRUE.
  • You will need to set rmc.doresample to TRUE because you exported the data without resampling, and GGIR wants a consistent sample rate throughout the recording.

Note that .cwa files are probably more compact to store than the compressed csv files, but I guess either way should be useful for research.

Regarding Jairo's comment - At some point I tried to facilitate Axivity csv format and it may still work, but I later  realised that OMGUI facilitates a lot of sub versions of csv format and it felt tricky to try to auto-detect all those variations. The read.myacc.csv route would seem more practical as you as a user will be in control of how the file is handled.

Best,

Vincent
